title: FP16 scaling and numerical instability probe (kernel + scheduler + KV cache)
content:
Purpose:
This note collects observations, hypotheses, and a prioritized test/mitigation plan for NaN/inf and result drift issues we're observing in production inference when using mixed-precision (fp16) kernels together with our KV cache and request scheduling heuristics. It's intended to be a working log for the runtime team to converge on concrete fixes and tests.

Summary of observed failure modes (field reports):
- Sporadic NaNs emitted from fused attention kernels during autoregressive generation. Failures are rare but cluster on long generation sequences (>1024) and when the scheduler colocates many short requests on the same GPU.
- Silent degradation (no NaN) where output logits slowly blow up and produce extremely skewed softmax (one token prob ~ 0.9999) after repeated rollouts. More visible when repetition penalty / temperature adjustments are applied by the client.
- Higher incidence of instability with quantized int8-backed kernels (offload path) vs our fp16-only path.
- KV cache accumulation patterns: some layers show steadily increasing max-abs activation for cached keys across time steps, even when inputs are stable.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Accumulation in fp16 reduction ops: reductions (sum, dot) are performed in fp16 in a few legacy kernels. Repeated addition of small fp16 values loses information and can cause underflow/overflow after many tokens.
2) Improper scaling / missing stable-softmax patterns in custom fused logits kernels (not subtracting max before exp) leading to occasional overflow in exp when logits grow (e.g., with repetition penalties or scaling applied repeatedly by scheduler).
3) Scheduler micro-batching & kernel reuse: our scheduler sometimes splits a long generation into many micro-batches that get repeatedly cast between fp16/fp32, causing rounding drift.
4) KV cache write ordering + fused GEMM rounding: cache write paths that append past-kv columns without an fp32 accumulation lead to drift in the kv matrices over long sequences.
5) Race condition in kernel implementation when using warp-level reductions + warp shuffle on new CUDA versions leading to nondeterministic NaNs in edge cases.

What we've checked so far (quick experiments):
- Replicated failing trace in local dev with SEQ=2048, batch=1, using our fused attention: getting NaN at token 1530. Turning off fusion (reference kernels) converts failure to a large value but not a NaN (hinting at a numerical edge in the fused path).
- Force-cast all accumulators to fp32 in an A/B build: no NaNs observed across 5/5 long-sequence trials, but runtime is ~12% slower on GPU X.
- Instrumented max-abs statistics per layer for cached keys: layer 10 shows monotonic increase in max-abs across time steps in failing trace.
- Reproduced higher failure rate when enabling temperature=0.5 + repetition-penalty=1.2 in sampling loop vs greedy decode.

Immediate mitigations for production (short-term):
- Telemetry: emit per-request non-finite counters (token-level). Add alert when >0.001% tokens are non-finite in a request window. (low-effort, high-ROI)
- Autosafe fallback: if a request sees a NaN on any token, automatically retry the request on fp32 variant of model (if available) and surface the original logits. Implement this as a transparent fallback in the scheduler.
- Clip logits before exp in fused kernels: clamp logits to +/- L where L is empirically set (e.g., +/- 80) to avoid overflow in exp. This is a bandaid but cheap.

Design-level mitigations (medium-term):
1) Enforce fp32 accumulation for reductions and GEMM epilogues across all kernels that participate in generation (+ unit tests). Specifically: dot-product accumulators, prefix-sum, softmax denominators should use fp32 accumulation and only cast the final result to fp16.
2) Softmax stability: require numerically stable softmax patterns in every fused logits kernel (subtract max, compute exp in fp32 accumulation where possible, sum in fp32).
3) KV cache storage: store KV as fp16 for memory, but maintain a shadow fp32 running-accumulator for layers where we detect growth (configurable per-model). This can be toggled per model profile.
4) Scheduler changes: avoid destructive repeated casting—batch requests such that each generation step is executed with consistent dtype choices. Add a 'dtype pinning' flag for a GPU queue so that all ops in a generation for pinned models remain in fp16/fp32 consistently.
5) Kernel CI: expand kernel testbed to run long-seq fuzzing under stress (SEQ up to 4096, random token sequences, sampling temperature variations) with deterministic seeding and memory sanitizer tools. Run nightly across driver versions and CUDA minor releases.

Proposed experiments and test plan (ordered):
A) Fast unit checks (dev workstation) - low cost, 1–3 days
  - Add per-op non-finite detectors to fused attention and run with sequences [512,1024,2048] across batch sizes [1,4]. Collect layer-wise first-NaN token index.
  - Run identical workloads with (i) fp16 base kernels, (ii) fp16 with fp32 accumulators, (iii) unfused reference kernels. Compare NaN incidence and max-abs activation growth.

B) Kernel microbench and profiling - medium cost, 3–5 days
  - Instrument CUDA kernels for max exponent argument passed to exp(), distribution of values, and per-warp reduction sanity. Use nvprof / Nsight to capture pathological launches.
  - Evaluate cost of switching accumulator to fp32 on critical kernels (latency and memory). Identify top-3 latency-sensitive kernels.

C) Scheduler stress matrix - medium cost, 4–7 days
  - Synthetic load generator: vary request interleaving and micro-batch co-location settings. Measure correlation between scheduler pattern and NaN incidence.
  - Implement 'dtype pinning' toggle and measure regression rate under same load matrix.

D) Long-run KV cache stability test - higher cost, 1–2 weeks
  - Run long-running generation workloads (background process) with randomized prompts and sampling, store per-step layer stats. Run both fp16-only and fp16+shadow-fp32 accumulator modes.

E) Regression & rollout plan - 2+ weeks
  - Bake fixes into a canary autoscaling fleet with telemetry to track non-finite token rate, invocation retries, and percent of requests falling back to fp32.
  - If residual instability persists beyond threshold, apply a rollout guard that routes high-risk models to fp32 by default while we continue kernel fixes.

Open implementation questions (engineering discussion items):
- Which kernels are allowed to use fp16 accumulation for performance reasons (e.g., convolution-style kernels where we can guarantee bounded dynamic range)? We need a whitelist vs a blacklist approach and a mechanism to mark kernel variants in the model profile catalog.
- How much latency can we accept for fp32 accumulators on tail-latency sensitive customers? Could we implement hybrid kernels where accumulation is fp32 but storage/outputs remain fp16?
- Operational cost: storing shadow fp32 accumulators per layer increases memory by ~2x for those layers. For dedicated customers this may be acceptable, but we need a pricing/feature flag.
- Scheduler complexity: dtype pinning reduces packing efficiency. We need a cost model (tokens/sec) trade-off to decide when to pin.

Action items (next 7 days, owners):
- Aisha: add non-finite per-token telemetry + alert hooks (PR: gh#412).
- Marco: prototype fp32-accumulator build for fused attention + microbench (branch: fp32-accum-probe).
- Lina: implement deterministic long-seq fuzz harness and add to nightly kernel CI.
- Samir: draft scheduler dtype-pinning design and perf model; run initial co-location stress experiments.

Appendix: quick checklist for kernel authors (copiable):
- Always apply stable softmax: logits = logits - max(logits) before exp.
- Use fp32 for reduction accumulators or Kahan compensated summation where appropriate.
- Clamp exp inputs to reasonable range (e.g., [-80, 80]) if using exp in fp16-only path.
- Add explicit non-finite checks at op boundaries and fail fast with telemetry.
- Include a debug build flag that forces casts to fp32 for suspect ops to aid repro.

Notes and stray observations:
- Some failing traces show the NaN originating immediately after a dynamic temperature adjust. Need to look at client-side adjustments that mutate logits in-place.
- Driver/CUDA version mismatch seems correlated with a small subset of failures. Add driver/version to telemetry and run CI across more driver permutations.

This doc is a living record — add experimental results, PR links, and updated timelines inline.
